match.reason: No bank point teaches writing off debts against an allowance for doubtful debts; the closest accounting card (Returns, bad debts and discounts) treats a bad debt as a direct expense, which is a different method.

draft.title: Writing off bad debts
card: At the end of a period, the business records an allowance for doubtful debts. This is an estimate of debts it expects not to collect, and the expense is recorded then.
In the next period, a customer may be known to be unable to pay. The business then writes off that debt as a bad debt.

The write-off debits Allowance for doubtful debts and credits Accounts receivable (and the customer's account). It is not a new expense, because the expense was recorded when the allowance was set up.
The write-off lowers both accounts receivable and the allowance by the same amount. The net amount expected to be collected stays the same.
draft.remember: The expense is recorded when the allowance is made. A write-off only uses up the allowance.

a.q: In the next period, Tran Traders writes off a customer's debt of $400 against its allowance. Which entry is made?
opts: Dr Allowance for doubtful debts, Cr Accounts receivable
Dr Bad debts expense, Cr Accounts receivable
Dr Accounts receivable, Cr Allowance for doubtful debts
Dr Bad debts expense, Cr Allowance for doubtful debts
a.why: The write-off removes the debt from accounts receivable and uses up part of the allowance. The expense was already recorded when the allowance was created, so debiting Bad debts expense again would count it twice.
a.clue: The expense was recorded in the previous period.

b.q: Kiah's Cycles has accounts receivable of $20,000 and an allowance of $1,500. It writes off a $600 debt against the allowance. What is the net amount expected to be collected afterwards?
opts: $18,500, the same as before the write-off
$17,900, which is $600 lower than before
$19,400, which is $600 higher than before
$18,500, which is $600 lower than before
b.why: Before, net receivables are $20,000 less $1,500, which is $18,500. After the write-off, receivables are $19,400 and the allowance is $900, so net is still $18,500. Option $17,900 wrongly treats the write-off as a new expense that lowers net receivables.
b.clue: Both accounts fall by the same amount.

a.best: Dr Allowance for doubtful debts, Cr Accounts receivable

b.best: $18,500, the same as before the write-off

problems.detail: "A write-off only uses up the allowance" uses "only" and leaves out that the write-off also lowers accounts receivable, which the card states. A student could read it as affecting the allowance alone.
